1.explanation: The Toggle component in 'Toggle.js' is the key element, as it is the implementation of the toggle UI and its logic. To add a read-only prop and associated styles/behavior, the core Toggle function must be updated to: (1) accept the new read-only prop, (2) prevent value changes when read-only is true, and (3) apply the appropriate className and aria attributes for accessibility. Stories and tests reference and wrap the Toggle component, but the main logic for handling the new prop is in the component itself. No other classes are present in the file. Supporting files like stories and tests would need changes, but the bug's core logic and behavior reside in the Toggle component/function.
1.bug_scenario: The bug scenario concerns adding a 'read-only' prop to the Toggle component. When the toggle is set to read-only (and not disabled), it should be accessible to screen readers but not allow the user to change its value. The acceptance criteria also require new styles for the read-only state, controls in the playground, an example story, and RTL tests for the read-only class. The scenario images show the various color, typography, and structure rules for toggles, but do not illustrate the 'read-only' state directly. Rather, they reinforce the need for correct visual and accessibility handling of all toggle states, including the new read-only state.

2.explanation: The core logic for the Toggle component is implemented in the Toggle function in packages/react/src/components/Toggle/Toggle.js. This is where a new 'readOnly' prop needs to be introduced, and logic added to prevent state changes when the toggle is read-only. This file and function handle rendering, event handling, and accessibility attributes, all of which must be updated for read-only support. Additional work would be needed in the stories and tests files, but the main bug fix logic belongs in the Toggle component itself.
2.bug_scenario: The bug relates to the Toggle component not supporting a read-only state. The requirement is to add a 'readOnly' prop, ensure proper styles for read-only state, have controls for each state in the playground, include a default story, and implement RTL (right-to-left) tests for the read-only class. When the toggle is read-only (and not disabled), it should be accessible to screen readers but not allow changing its value.
